name: ATR 42 / ATR 72
summary: High-wing twin turboprop; in the US flown mainly as FedEx Feeder freighters by Mountain Air Cargo and Empire Airlines.

wings: High-mounted straight wing with slight taper
Engine nacelles slung under the wing
engines: Two Pratt & Whitney Canada PW120-series turboprops
Four-blade props on older 42/72s, six-blade composite props on -500/-600
fuselage: Long slender fuselage with an upswept rear
Main landing gear retracts into blister fairings on the lower fuselage sides, not the engine nacelles
Freighters have no cabin windows and a large forward cargo door
tail: T-tail with a tall swept fin and dorsal fillet

tellTales: High wing with a T-tail on a twin-turboprop airliner
Main-gear blisters on the lower fuselage sides
Slim engine nacelles hanging under the wing

confusedWith.howToTell: The ATR is a much larger pressurized airliner with retractable gear and a T-tail; the Twin Otter has a strut-braced wing, fixed gear and a low tail.
The ATR has a high wing; the 1900 has a low wing with engines on top of it and small fins on the rear fuselage.
The ATR has two engines and a T-tail; the C-130 has four engines, a low tail and an upswept rear loading ramp.

usCount.source: FedEx Feeder operator fleet data (Mountain Air Cargo 23, Empire Airlines 18, others; Mountain Air Cargo / ch-aviation)
